# a. Use only the numerical variables (1 to 9) to cluster the 21 firms.

# Load the Dataset
```{r}
Pharma <- read.csv("~/ML/Pharmaceuticals.csv")

head(Pharma)
str(Pharma)
summary(Pharma)
dim(Pharma)
```

# Extract the numerical variables
```{r}
Pharma_numeric <- Pharma[, 3:11]

# View selected variables

head(Pharma_numeric)

```
#Check for missing values 
```{r}
sum(is.na(Pharma_numeric))
```
#Scale the variables
```{r}
# Standardize numerical variables
Pharma_scaled <- scale(Pharma_numeric)

# View standardized data
head(Pharma_scaled)
```


#Run K-Means for k=2,3 and 4
```{r}

set.seed(123)

k2 <- kmeans(Pharma_scaled,
             centers = 2,
             nstart = 25)

k3 <- kmeans(Pharma_scaled,
             centers = 3,
             nstart = 25)

k4 <- kmeans(Pharma_scaled,
             centers = 4,
             nstart = 25)
```

# Add Cluster labels to the Dataset
```{r}
Pharma$Cluster_k2 <- k2$cluster
Pharma$Cluster_k3 <- k3$cluster
Pharma$Cluster_k4 <- k4$cluster

# View company cluster assignments
head(Pharma)
```
# Compute Cluster Summaries for K = 2

```{r}
aggregate(Pharma_numeric,
          by = list(Cluster = k2$cluster),
          FUN = mean)
```
# For K = 3
# Calculate average values 
```{r}
aggregate(Pharma_numeric,
          by = list(Cluster = k3$cluster),
          FUN = mean)
```
#Count companies in each cluster
```{r}
table(k3$cluster)
```
# K = 4
## Calculate average values for each cluster
```{r}

aggregate(Pharma_numeric,
          by = list(Cluster = k4$cluster),
          FUN = mean)
```
# Count companies
```{r}
table(k4$cluster)
```

# Clustering Method Justification

I selected the nine numerical variables for clustering and excluded the categorical variables. I standardized the variables using the `scale()` function because they have different measurement scales. This gives each variable equal weight in the clustering process.

I used the K-Means algorithm with `nstart = 25` to obtain reliable clustering results. I tested 2, 3, and 4 clusters to compare different groupings and identify the most suitable number of clusters.

#b. Interpret the clusters with respect to the numerical variables used in forming the clusters
# Calculate cluster averages for K = 3

```{r}
cluster_summary <- aggregate(
  Pharma_numeric,
  by = list(Cluster = k3$cluster),
  FUN = mean
)

round(cluster_summary, 2)
```
# The cluster averages help us understand how the companies differ in terms of their financial performance, profitability, growth, and risk.

#c. Is there a pattern in the clusters with respect to the numerical variables (10 to 12)? (those not used in forming the clusters)



```{r}
#Recreate the cluster vector

set.seed(123)

k3 <- kmeans(Pharma_scaled, centers = 3, nstart = 25)

#Add the cluster label to the pharma

Pharma$Cluster_k3 <- k3$cluster

length(Pharma$Cluster_k3)
```

```{r}

#Check the pattern in categorical variables
table(Pharma$Cluster_k3, Pharma$Median_Recommendation)

table(Pharma$Cluster_k3, Pharma$Location)

table(Pharma$Cluster_k3, Pharma$Exchange)
```
# Compare the numerical variables 10–12

```{r}
cluster_summary_10_12 <- aggregate(
  Pharma[, 12:14],
  by = list(Cluster = Pharma$Cluster_k3),
  FUN = mean
)

round(cluster_summary_10_12, 2)
```

# d. Provide an appropriate name for each cluster using any or all of the variables in the dataset.


Cluster 1 – Mixed Recommendation Companies. They have different recommendations, such as Hold, Moderate Buy, and Strong Buy. They are also located in different countries.

Cluster 2 – Large US-Based Companies. Most companies in this group are from the US and listed on the NYSE. Most of them received a Hold recommendation.

Cluster 3 – International Growth Companies. This group includes companies from France, Ireland, and the US. They are listed on different stock exchanges and have different recommendations.

Brief Clarification:

I named each cluster based on its main characteristics. Cluster 2 mostly includes US-based companies listed on the NYSE, while Clusters 1 and 3 have a mix of locations and recommendations, making them more diverse groups.
